gaps.explanation: 'Several charges' means more than two; the other options are used only with uncountable nouns.

gaps.sentence: There are ___ than forty applicants for every training place.
gaps.explanation: 'More than' + number expresses quantities above a figure.
'Neither of my parents is ...' is correct for two items with a singular verb; 'both/all' need a plural verb and 'none' is not used for two.

gaps.sentence: A large ___ of students have applied this year.
gaps.explanation: 'A large number of students' is used with countable plurals; 'amount' is for uncountables.

gaps.sentence: There was ___ enthusiasm for the proposal, so it was quietly shelved.
gaps.explanation: 'Little' (without 'a') means not enough — which explains shelving the proposal.

gaps.sentence: Don't rush — we've got ___ of time.
gaps.hint: fixed pattern: ___ of time (no article needed)
gaps.explanation: 'Plenty of time' needs no article; 'lot of time' would need 'a', and 'much of time' needs 'the'.

gaps.sentence: ___ the food was eaten within minutes.
gaps.explanation: 'All the food' is correct with an uncountable noun; 'whole' needs 'the whole of' and 'both' needs two separate items.

gaps.sentence: How ___ sugar do you take in your coffee?
gaps.explanation: 'Much' is used with uncountable nouns like sugar; 'many' is for countable plurals.
